newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Setback for De Beers' India plans - paper.
newsitem.headline: Setback for De Beers' India plans - paper.

text.p: De Beers has suffered a setback in its plans to prospect for diamonds in Madhya Pradesh province in India, after the provincial government backtracked on a decision to allocate the company a lease for the region, Business Day newspaper said on Friday.

The newspaper said the province had decided to amend its tender for the lease following widespread protests by the opposition Hindu nationalist party, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) against De Beers receiving the lease.
The BJP staged a protest in parliament late last year against the presence of foreign mining companies and demanded the lease be withdrawn, the paper said.
The province is shortly expected to call for a new tender, the paper said. The tender would be limited to local Indian companies which could, however, team up with foreign mining groups, it said.
De Beers has an agreement to set up a joint venture with India's Reliance Industries Ltd, said to be estimated at $30 million, to mine diamonds in the region, Business Day said.

The South African diamond company's original bid for the lease followed the Madhya Pradesh government's global tender in 1994, the paper said. Reports said De Beers had been one of three companies shortlisted in this tender.
The paper quoted De Beers' spokesman Andrew Cumine as saying the company was considering prospecting for diamonds in other regions in India, including Crissa and Andhra Pradesh provinces.
